title: Vocabulary & Language
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah memiliki pengetahuan dasar untuk menceritakan tempat liburan dan alat transportasi yang pernah mereka gunakan.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 72-74
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will learn new vocabulary about going on vacation (places to visit and ways to travel).
Learners will be able to understand, identify, and say key vocabulary about going on vacation.
Learners will be able to ask and answer questions about vacations in the past using the past simple (did + base verb, went, stayed, took).

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures and questions on page 72.

Put students into groups of 3-4 and ask them to talk about what they can see in the pictures (e.g. people on a boat, people putting up a tent). Tell them to write down any English words they know about vacations in their notebooks.
Elicit some ideas from the groups and write down any key words on the board.
Read the questions on the page together and model your own answers as a guide, for example: “I went on vacation to Bali with my family. We swam in the ocean and saw lots of fish.”
Tell students they have 5-6 minutes to discuss the questions. Encourage them to use English, but if they don’t have enough vocabulary, it’s acceptable to use some words in their first language.
After 5-6 minutes, stop the task and elicit some ideas from students.
Tell students not to worry if the questions were difficult. By the end of Unit 9, they will be able to talk about their past vacations more easily.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 73 and ask the class, “What can you see on the page?”
Tell students that they will do a listening task. They need to listen and write the number in each box according to the order they hear the words in the audio.
Before playing the audio, read all of the words together: travel by plane, go by boat, ride the train, take the bus, the beach, the mountains, a resort, go camping.
Play audio 9.1. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to do the task. Then, continue with the audio.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, then play the audio again.
Check the answers together. Write the correct answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Ask students to read the sentences from the audio script aloud, in pairs (e.g. “We go by boat to the island because there is no other way to get there.”).
This activity is for pronunciation practice.
Tell students to listen and repeat the words they hear.

Play audio 9.2 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly, and encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio. Check to make sure all students are repeating the vocabulary.
Pay attention to the phrases with two or three words (e.g. travel by plane, ride the train) so students say them smoothly as one chunk.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
Ask students to look in their books at the Vocabulary C task and check if students understand the task, e.g., Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Do the first number together as a class to make sure students understand what to do.
Put students in pairs and ask them to complete the sentences with the vocabulary from Vocabulary A in around 8 minutes.
Remind students to check the verb form in each sentence, for example “She goes to the beach” and “He rides the train”.
Then, check the answers. Write the answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Ask students to read the completed sentences aloud to each other, in pairs.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Write one question for each key word on the board or show them on a screen, for example:
Do you like to go camping with your friends or family?
How often do you ride the train to school or to the city?
What do you like to do when you go to the beach?
When did you last travel by plane, and where did you go?
Have you ever stayed at a resort during a holiday?
Do you usually take the bus when you go around your city?
Ask students to write the questions in their notebooks. Then put them in pairs to ask and answer the questions and write their partner’s answers.
Give around 10-12 minutes and make sure that every student practices both asking and answering.
Elicit answers from the class or ask several students to write one answer on the board, then correct any mistakes together as a class.
Ask students to open their Student Book to page 74.
First, the teacher reads the Q&A models in the speech bubbles at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the Q&A models aloud as a class.
Then, the teacher asks students to read the Q&A models together in pairs (Read with a friend).

Highlight the key structure (past simple): “Where did you go on vacation?” – “I went to the mountains.”, “Did you stay at a hotel?” – “No, we didn’t. We stayed at a resort.”, “How did you get there?” – “We took a train.”
Point out that we use did + base verb in questions (Did you stay …? not Did you stayed …?) and the past form in answers (went, stayed, took).

This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs. Encourage students to change the key vocabulary in the questions and answers, by using the vocabulary learned on the previous page.
Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes). This can be used to help answer students' questions.
Ask students to look at the practice task B on Student Book page 74 and ask, “What can you see in the pictures?”
Read the example (number 1) aloud together as a class.

Students complete the questions and answers with the correct form of the verbs (e.g. did / go – went, Did / stay – didn’t stay / stayed, Did / take – took, did / get – took). Remind students to use the Q&A models and the Language Box to help guide them.
Put students in pairs and give them around 6-8 minutes to complete the task.
Ask students to check their answers with a new partner, then check the answers. Write the answers on the board.
Ask students to take turns reading the questions and answers aloud. Student A asks and Student B answers, then switch roles.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Students ask each other about their last vacation, following the Q&A models at the top of Student Book page 74. They can give real information or be creative.
Write the following conversation frame on the board:
Q: Where did you go on vacation last year?
A: My family and I ________ on vacation last year.
Q: Did you stay at ________ last year?
A: Yes / No, we ________ last year.
Q: How did you get to ________?
A: We ________ to ________ last year.
Put students in pairs and ask them to practice the conversation twice so each student can both ask and answer.
Then put students in different pairs and ask them to repeat the task, changing the time phrase (e.g. last month, last week).
Give corrective feedback by writing some common mistakes on the board (e.g. “Where did you went?”, “She taked a train.”) and asking students to correct them.
Choose 1-2 students to share where they went on their last vacation and how they got there, using the past simple (e.g. “I went to the beach. We took the bus.”).
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: pengamatan pelafalan saat drill kosakata (listen and repeat).
Pemeriksaan jawaban latihan kosakata dan language practice di Student Book.
Unjuk kerja lisan: peserta didik memakai kosakata & struktur baru dalam kalimat sendiri.

Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
